chapter_title: Chương 28: 0028 【Tìm vật tín của Tần Thủy Hoàng】

segments.title: Chương 28: 0028 【Tìm vật tín của Tần Thủy Hoàng】
segments.content:
When I woke up, the sky was already bright.

The moment Chen Guiliang opened his eyes, he saw the light shining through the tiles of the roof.

His family's house had earthen walls and a tile roof. It was common for it to be drafty and leaky; during a downpour, they even needed to use buckets and basins to catch the water.

It was supposed to have been rebuilt into a two-story house several years ago, but the project had been delayed because his father was swindled.

There wasn't even any decent furniture; it was all old stuff from when his parents got married, either bought by them or part of the dowry.

Lying in bed, Chen Guiliang began to think about renovating the house.

If he bought a house in a big city, his grandmother most likely wouldn't be used to it.

Besides, his grandmother got carsick.

He could wait until after he started a business in university to earn money for a new house.

The most urgent task was to study hard for the review, get into a good university, and bring honor to his parents, grandmother, and maternal grandparents.

This was extremely important.

Not counting junior colleges, the village had only produced one university student so far, who became a doctor at a hospital in the provincial capital after graduating. That family was highly respected because of it, and no matter what happened, the village neighbors would proactively help them out.

Although villagers would help each other out in ordinary families too, the treatment that family received was clearly different.

Chen Guiliang had the ability to become the second university student in the entire village!

Grandma and the others would definitely be happy.

Guaranteed admission through competitions wasn't a sure thing. Chen Guiliang had to have a backup plan and diligently improve his academic scores.

"Grandma, Grandma!"

Chen Guiliang got out of bed and called out a few times, discovering that his grandmother was outside feeding the chickens.

The family's farmland had already been "given" to the neighbors to cultivate, leaving only two private plots for growing vegetables.

It was the complete opposite of ancient landlords recruiting tenants; now, you were actually indebted to someone for "giving" away your land. Because if the land lay fallow for a few years, by the time Chen Guiliang's parents came home, they would have to put in a lot of effort to reclaim it if they wanted to farm again.

Furthermore, as more and more people left to work elsewhere, the amount of fallow land in the village increased year by year. Only those on good terms with you would be willing to "help" you farm your land.

The grain grown in the fields naturally belonged to the actual cultivators.

But the agricultural taxes had to be paid by the original landowner!

Grandma could never stay idle. Besides tending to the private plots, she went out to cut firewood every day and also raised a lot of poultry.

"The food is in the pot!" Grandma shouted.

Chen Guiliang went to the kitchen to get the food, and Grandma also sat down at the table after feeding the chickens and ducks.

Porridge and pickled vegetables.

After breakfast, Grandma barely rested before going to weed the vegetable plots.

Chen Guiliang followed her and said, "Grandma, we have enough firewood to last for years. You don't have to go out and cut firewood. You're climbing up and down slopes. What if you slip and fall?"

Grandma said, "Okay."

Chen Guiliang said no more, nor did he help her pull weeds.

He knew his grandmother was just too idle and looking for something to do. If he helped her pull all the weeds now, she would definitely go find some other work.

It was as if the farm work was endless, always popping up from somewhere.

"Ge!"

His cousin Chen Guirong stood in the courtyard and called out.

Chen Guiliang walked over with a smile, "You've grown taller again."

Chen Guirong sat on the threshold, looking rather helpless. "It's finally the weekend, and I was planning to hang out with my classmates. But my dad insisted I come over to ask you for study tips. With my grades, what damn tips are there to ask for?"

His cousin was in the third year of junior high this year, and his academic performance was abysmal. He would only be able to get into a trashy high school.

Later, he didn't even graduate from high school, dropping out to attend a technical school. He did quite well as a chef and even became a minor internet celebrity by making cooking videos.

"Ge, do you have any cigarettes?" Chen Guirong asked in a low voice.

Chen Guiliang said, "No."

"I heard you were handing out Hongtashan cigarettes everywhere yesterday," Chen Guirong said.

Chen Guiliang reminded him, "You're a minor."

Chen Guirong thought to himself: You're only turning eighteen next year yourself.

Chen Guiliang asked again, "Is your school still as chaotic as it was?"

Seeing that he couldn't bum a cigarette, his cousin had to give up. "Ge, did you forget? There was a city-wide crackdown last year, police were arresting people everywhere. The school is very peaceful now."

Chen Guiliang instantly recalled it. The city's TV station had even broadcasted the results of the crackdown, displaying rows upon rows of firearms, knives, and steel pipes.

Hundreds, if not thousands, of miscellaneous criminals and gangsters had been arrested.

The nationwide "Strike Hard Campaign" in '01 and '02 naturally didn't exclude Longdu City.

Chen Guirong chuckled. "Actually, even without the crackdown, as long as I mention your name, those thugs wouldn't dare to mess with me."

After chatting with his cousin for a while, Chen Guiliang wandered around the house.

Finally, in an empty pigsty that wasn't being used, he found a few empty beverage bottles his grandmother had picked up.

"Come with me." Chen Guiliang picked up a Sprite bottle and headed for the riverbank a few hundred meters away.

Chen Guirong chased after him, asking, "Ge, what are you doing?"

Chen Guiliang said something his cousin couldn't understand: "Qin Shi Huang needs a token."

"Qin Shi Huang?" Chen Guirong scratched his head.

The small river in front of their house had made a great contribution during the War of Resistance.

At that time, the salt-producing regions in the coastal provinces were occupied by those damn Japanese devils. The salt produced in Longdu City had to supply several surrounding provinces, making it the most important salt-producing area in the great rear of the war.

Much of that salt was transported out through this small river, and a nearby salt transport dock had even been bombed.

On the riverbank, as far as the eye could see, there were only pebbles.

Chen Guiliang drilled a hole in the middle of the Sprite bottle cap, then filled the bottle with river water. He said to his cousin, "Help me find some small, good-looking pebbles."

"What are you looking for pebbles for?" Chen Guirong asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "A gift for a girl."

"Hahaha!"

Chen Guirong immediately laughed at him. "Ge, you're so old-fashioned. Who gives girls pebbles? You'll definitely be looked down on for this."

"What the hell do you know."

When Chen Guiliang was a student, he always felt that you needed money to be in a relationship. A gift worth only a few yuan was too cheap and embarrassing; he couldn't bring himself to give something like that.

But having been reborn, he dared to give away a worthless broken stone.

Despite his ridicule, his cousin still obediently squatted down and helped him search for pretty pebbles.

"How about this one?" Chen Guirong picked one up.

Chen Guiliang used the Sprite bottle to spray water, washing away the mud and sand from the pebble's surface. "Nope. It has cracks, and it's too big."

Tossing away the broken stone, Chen Guirong started searching again. As he searched, he said, "Ge, you should let me teach you how to pick up girls. Your methods are long outdated."

"You're already dating in junior high?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Chen Guirong said, "What's wrong with dating in junior high?"

Chen Guiliang said, "How do you guys date?"

"Take a girl to play on the computer. There are internet cafes in town now, it's just a shame they can't connect to the internet," Chen Guirong said. "And rollerblading. A rollerblading rink opened in town. They blast Jay Chou's songs over the big speakers, and it's super stylish when you skate. I even dyed my hair blond a while back, I was so damn handsome. Sigh, but I got a beating from my dad when I got home, so I had to spend money to dye it back."

"Serves you right for getting beaten!"

"Ge, look, is this one okay?"

"It's too gaudy, the colors are a mess."

"How about we go to the city and pick out a bracelet for your girl... I mean, for my sister-in-law? You know, the crystal kind, they sparkle and are fucking beautiful!"

"Shut up and just keep looking!"

The warm sun of an early winter morning shone on the two boys on the riverbank.

After being busy for a full hour, the two brothers had selected over thirty pebbles.

Chen Guiliang took them to the riverbank to wash them all, comparing them again and again, one by one.

In the end, he kept one and threw the rest into the river.

Back home, Grandma was gone again. She had probably finished weeding and gone off somewhere to find more farm work to do.

Chen Guiliang lit the firewood to boil water and said to his cousin, "Go catch a chicken."

"You got it!"

Grandma was too frugal. She was reluctant to buy meat and reluctant to kill the chickens.

As noon approached, Grandma returned carrying a bundle of firewood to find her two grandsons had slaughtered one of her egg-laying hens.

"Grandma, the chicken is stewing in the pot. It'll be ready in about half an hour," his cousin said with a grin.

Grandma smiled too and went to the main room to turn on the TV.

She liked this color television.

Chen Guiliang had his cousin continue to tend the fire while he went to watch TV with Grandma. "Grandma, when I come back next time, I'll buy you a kitten. You can play with the cat at home, don't go out looking for work to keep yourself busy."

Grandma made a request: "I want a native cat, one that can catch mice."

"Then I'll buy a black and white one," Chen Guiliang said.

Grandma didn't really like visiting the neighbors. When she ran into the old ladies in the village, she was usually the one listening while others talked.

Raising a lively tuxedo cat would surely make life more interesting.

Estimating the time, Grandma went to the kitchen, lifted the pot lid, and poked the stewing chicken with chopsticks. "It's not ready yet, needs to stew a bit longer. Rongrong, take a bowl back with you at noon."

His cousin smiled. "Okay."

Although the two families didn't get along very well because of his grandfather and second aunt, they still had to maintain basic interactions.

For example, if one family made a meat dish, they would send a bowl over to the other.

But his second aunt also had a countermeasure. Every time she bought meat, she would only buy a very small amount, which would only make a small plate when cooked, making it awkward for his second uncle to offer to bring some to Grandma.

Once the chicken was done, his cousin ladled out a bowl. "Grandma, Ge, I'm heading out."

"Watch where you're going, don't fall," Grandma reminded him.

"I know, I know." Chen Guirong left at a trot.

After his cousin was long gone, Chen Guiliang took out five hundred yuan. "Grandma, this is from my dad. The whole village knows my dad's struck it rich, so someone will definitely come to borrow money, and we might also attract thieves."

"I know better than you do." Grandma took the money and went to the inner room to hide it.

When the elderly encountered a thief at home, they would usually just lie down and pretend to be asleep. The thief would rummage through chests and cupboards and leave whether they found money or not.

Two years ago, the chickens and ducks Grandma was raising were all stolen one night by a gang of thieves.

She had realized it at the time and had even recognized who the thieves were.

But she didn't dare to shout, she could only continue to sleep.

When the retired police chief of our town had a burglar at night, he also just lay there pretending to be asleep, even snoring. The next day, he leisurely went to the station to report the crime, pointing out who had come to his house to steal things. When you need to be a coward, be a coward. There's no need to be a hero!!

After lunch, and after watching another half-hour of TV with his grandmother, Chen Guiliang got up to pack his things and said, "Grandma, I'm going to school."

"Let's go, I'll see you off." Grandma turned off the TV.

Chen Guiliang brought his first-year and second-year high school textbooks and walked with his grandmother, one behind the other, towards the village road.

"Grandma, you don't have to see me off any further."

"Okay, you go on then."

Chen Guiliang walked along the village road for a while, then turned to look back and saw his grandmother was still standing on the hillside.

He knew that only when he had crossed over the mountain pass and was completely out of sight would his grandmother be at ease and head home.
